transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-11
Start time: 15:00 PT
Duration: 34 minutes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Alex (OceanWide Eng Manager), Sam (InfoSec), Dana (Legal), Rita (Product)

Summary: Quick product walkthrough focusing on request storage toggles, automated PII redaction, console-based guardrails, and relevant security controls. Customer wants to understand: how to prevent storing PII, how toggles affect latency and logging, and what compliance artifacts we provide.

00:00 Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh we're gonna run through the request storage settings and how you can set up guardrails from both the console and API, uh feel free to jump in.
00:18 Alex: thanks, Jordan, quick ask up front - Sam and Dana are here for security/legal so we'll pepper questions as we go.
00:27 Priya: perfect, i'll start in the console, show the per-route toggles, then switch to API headers for ephemeral mode, and finally a small optimize note about batching/latency tradeoffs when redaction is enabled.
00:39 Sam: sounds good. first question: does turning off request storage remove everything from disk immediately or is it just excluded from future writes?
00:52 Priya: good question. the toggle 'request storage' in the console has three modes: persistent, ephemeral, and manual. persistent stores requests according to your retention policy; ephemeral keeps them in-memory only for the duration of the model session and is not written to long-term storage; manual means we persist but apply redaction and retention rules. when you pick ephemeral we do not write request payloads to our blob storage or audit pipeline, but we still emit minimal telemetry for billing and error tracing, and that telemetry is non-user-content.
01:30 Sam: non-user-content meaning tokens and latency metrics?
01:33 Priya: yep, token counts, latency histograms, error codes—those are safe. we don't log the prompt or the model output in ephemeral.
01:45 Dana: legal wants to confirm chain of custody - is there any intermediate caching that could leak PII? e.g., KV cache?
01:55 Priya: the K V cache (sometimes transcribed as K V) is per-instance in memory and not persisted for ephemeral mode. for persistent mode we persist cache snapshots for warm starts but those can be encrypted with customer-managed keys if you're on Private or Dedicated.
02:12 Jordan: quick demo, i'll share my screen - console > projects > oceanwide-pilot > routes > /checkout-bot.
02:23 [screen share noise]
02:30 Priya: okay on the route config page you can see the 'Request Storage' card - dropdown with the three modes i mentioned, plus a per-tenant override. note we also expose a per-route regex redaction list and a PII auto-detection toggle which uses our redact pipeline to remove names, SSNs, emails before persisting.
02:52 Alex: is the PII detection ML-based or rule-based?
02:56 Priya: both. we run a fast regex pass for common patterns and a secondary ML classifier for contextual PII like names in free-text. the ML pass is optional and adds a small CPU cost during persistence. in ephemeral mode it's not relevant since we don't persist.
03:14 Sam: how accurate is the ML pass? we need low false negatives.
03:18 Priya: accuracy varies by entity type. for emails/SSNs/credit cards regex is near 99% for standard formatting. for names or custom identifiers it's around 90-ish depending on your data; we recommend you also provide a custom dictionary for domain-specific PII.
03:34 Rita: can we redact at the token-level or replace with a stable pseudonym?
03:39 Priya: yes, options: full redaction (remove), mask with [REDACTED], or pseudonymize with deterministic hashing. pseudonymization is available with customer keys for Private deployments.
03:51 Dana: does pseudonymization count as personal data under our privacy counsel? we need to ensure it's reversible only with our key.
03:58 Priya: reversible pseudonymization is only supported with BYOK (bring-your-own-key) in Dedicated/Private. Redwood's hosted ephemeral/persistent modes offer deterministic hashing but we cannot store your key unless you're on Private and provide KMS/HSM integration.
04:18 Jordan: switching to API usage - there's an HTTP header and a parameter: X-Redwood-Storage-Mode: ephemeral|persistent|manual. you can also set per-request redaction flags e.g. X-Redwood-Redact: pii,custom.
04:33 Alex: if we call ephemeral in a streaming scenario, do we still get streaming outputs?
04:38 Priya: yes, streaming is independent. you can stream tokens and still use ephemeral. what you can't do is rely on that stream data being captured for post-hoc audits.
04:47 Sam: what about audit logs? we need an audit trail of who triggered which change, even if content is ephemeral.
04:53 Priya: audit logs are separate. changes to config, who toggled ephemeral, RBAC events are all written to the audit log; content is not included. audit logs can be integrated with your SIEM via syslog/forwarder.
05:06 Jordan: also note per-route rollout policies - you can willary ephemeral for 10% of requests while persistent remains for the rest, so you can validate behavior.
05:18 Alex: interesting. how does this impact cost? ephemeral seems cheaper from storage but maybe more expensive in compute if you don't cache.
05:26 Priya: tradeoff: ephemeral disables persistent caching and long-term KV snapshots, so warm-start benefits are reduced, which can increase token-level latency for cold sessions. our Redwood Optimize tool can recommend batching/quant profiles to offset that. we can run a quick estimate during pilot.
05:43 Dana: data residency - can we force storage to eu-west region only?
05:47 Priya: yes, for persistent mode you can pin storage region. for Private we deploy fully into your VPC region. ephemeral mode still processes in a selected region but since not persisted, residency for long-term storage isn't applicable.
05:59 Sam: show me the RBAC model for who can toggle request storage in console.
06:03 Priya: sure - screen share again.
06:10 Priya: roles: owner, admin, dev, auditor. only owner/admin can change global defaults; route-level roles allow devs to flip toggles for their services but auditor role is read-only. we also support SAML SSO and SCIM user sync so you can map groups.
06:26 Sam: do we have logs for RBAC changes and SSO events?
06:29 Priya: yes, those are part of the audit trail with timestamps, IP, and actor. we can forward to your SIEM.
06:35 Jordan: quick objection handling - if you compare us to ManagedCloudAI, they require per-request flags but their redaction is rule-only; we offer ML-enhanced redaction and pseudonymization for Private.
06:50 Alex: any compliance artifacts? we need SOC2, ISO, and encryption attestations.
06:54 Jordan: yes SOC2 Type II and ISO 27001 are available. i'll send the security pack after this call. (link: security-pack.pdf)
07:04 Dana: legal will want the exact wording about ephemeral - something that confirms we can request deletion of any persisted data.
07:10 Priya: for persisted data we support manual deletion APIs and retention windows; for ephemeral mode there is no persisted content to delete. i'll include the API delete endpoints in the docs.
07:22 Alex: can we run a demo where we intentionally send sample PII and see redaction happen?
07:28 Priya: yes let's do a quick live send from the API playground. i'll switch to the playground. 07:33
07:33 [brief pause]
07:38 Priya: i'm posting a sample prompt with a name and SSN - mode set to manual with regex + ML redaction.
07:45 Server: request received, processing...
07:51 Priya: result shows masked SSN and name replaced with [REDACTED_NAME]. note the transcript shows a redaction note in the entry and the persisted snapshot contains the masked output.
08:05 Alex: i see, can we audit the redaction decisions? like why was that token flagged?
08:11 Priya: yes there's an internal redaction.log that records detection type (regex vs ML), confidence score, and rule id; that log is included in your retention package but it does not include the original content for ephemeral mode.
08:24 Sam: what's retention package?
08:26 Priya: when you request exports for compliance we provide a retention export which includes metadata, audit events, redaction decisions, and optionally pseudonymized content. the actual original user content is only in persistent mode and only for the retention window you specify.
08:40 Alex: are there rate limits or throttles when we enable ML redaction?
08:44 Priya: small CPU overhead - we don't throttle per se but if your throughput is very high we may recommend Dedicated capacity with autoscaling to keep latency targets.
08:55 Jordan: i want to call out a practical thing: if you need deterministic pseudonyms for downstream analytics we can do that in Private with your KMS; that preserves referential integrity without exposing raw values.
09:09 Dana: okay legal will follow-up on reversible vs irreversible pseudonymization wording.
09:14 Priya: final part - console UI can enforce a policy: block any route from switching to persistent without an owner approval workflow. you can configure approvals so changes create a pending ticket that an owner must accept.
09:29 Alex: that's useful. how are policy changes tracked for audit?
09:33 Priya: tracked in audit logs with full diffs and previous value.
09:37 Jordan: time check, we have ten minutes left - Priya will walk through the sandbox steps to try ephemeral and we'll agree next steps.
09:45 Priya: ok i'll show the sandbox toggle. in the sandbox account i have a demo route; you can flip storage to ephemeral and then call via the api playground. i'm going to enable ephemeral now. 09:56
09:56 [switching screens]
10:02 Priya: toggled. now i'll call the endpoint with a sample prompt containing name/email and set X-Redwood-Redact: pii.
10:15 Server: got request - ephemeral mode - not persisted.
10:20 Alex: and where will error traces go if something fails?
10:23 Priya: error traces go to our error tracker with request id, but the content isn't included in ephemeral. we can forward the trace meta to your Sentry or equivalent.
10:32 Sam: one last question on backups - do you have backups of ephemeral memory snapshots for disaster recovery?
10:38 Priya: no backups for ephemeral - it's by definition transient. for persistent we have encrypted backups with configurable retention.
10:46 Jordan: wrap-up - to recap: ephemeral mode avoids persistence and is best for sensitive flows; manual mode allows redaction rules + audits; persistent mode if you need long-term storage and analytics. we support BYOK for pseudonymization in Private/Dedicated, RBAC, SAML/SCIM, and audit forwarding.
11:08 Dana: that covers our legal/security questions for now. we'll need the exact SLA language for deletion & retention.
11:15 Jordan: i'll include that in the security pack i send.
11:19 Alex: next steps sound good - can we do a pilot with 3 routes and 5k monthly requests with ephemeral and redaction enabled?
11:26 Jordan: yes we'll scope pricing; Priya will enable sandbox flags and we'll schedule the pilot kickoff the week of 2026-06-22.
11:34 Priya: action items again: enable sandbox flag, share docs, and we'll coordinate sample prompts.
11:40 [end]

Attachments/links mentioned: [security-pack.pdf], [ephemeral-api-playbook.md], [redaction-rule-examples.csv]
